info: J. J. Thomson proposed an early atomic model known as the Thomson Model or Plum Pudding Model. In this model, the atom was described as a sphere of positive charge spread uniformly throughout its volume, with negatively charged electrons embedded within it. The model did not include a central nucleus. The total positive charge balanced the total negative charge of the electrons, making the atom electrically neutral.

questions.questionText: How was positive charge distributed in Thomson's atomic model?

options: The total positive and negative charges balanced each other
